title: Genesis Primitives are permanently sealed after their single Invocation, not merely left idle
content:
For each of Pattern's four Genesis Primitives, the In Progress Invocations Directory is not empty-but-open — it is declared closed. A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.1.4: "Because the Agent Creation Primitive is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked." The same sentence recurs for Prime Transformation (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.1.4), Executor Transformation (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.3.1.4) and, adapted, for the Agent Token Primitive (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.1.4).

The corresponding Operational Process Definitions are closed the same way: "no further operational process is needed post-deployment" (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.3.1.2, A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.3.1.2).

The distinction being drawn is between *unused* and *unusable*. An idle primitive is a latent capability someone could invoke later; a sealed one has had that path removed. Creation and transformation are identity-defining events, and allowing a second Invocation would mean an Agent could be re-created or re-typed after the fact, invalidating every downstream reference that assumed a fixed identity.

This is why the Genesis/Operational split in the Primitive taxonomy matters structurally rather than just descriptively: Genesis Primitives are one-shot and self-sealing, Operational Primitives (like the Executor Accord) keep their Invocation path open indefinitely.
description: Pattern's Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation and Agent Token Primitives each declare that no further Instances can ever be Invoked, closing the one-time act by construction.
